why: Both made the same correct one-line wrap and the same function_call-history fix, but B also found and fixed a second real break A shipped past — Router's translated stream emits the role chunk alone, so with the default STREAM=true a plugin turn returned an empty reply and never ran the plugin; A's 200-only probe was structurally blind to it. On system judgment B uses more of the actual Router surface (proven fallback fall-through against a live 403, bounded provider_timeout against the 660s ceiling, spend label, per-chat prompt_cache_key measured -45% with a proper no-key control) and attacks the real structural gates (the 2024 model tables that make 80 of 100 catalog models unstartable, and billing users from usage.cost instead of a flat TOKEN_PRICE), where A's best work is a well-measured but narrower model-swap menu plus a conclusion that caching needed nothing.
A_best: Outstanding measurement discipline on model economics, including two findings an expert would miss: gpt-4o-mini bills 8,522 input tokens for the image gpt-4o bills 277 for (so the obvious vision downgrade costs more), and gpt-6-luna is a reasoning model at +2.3s to first token with a real crash path on content=None under a tight output cap — plus the correctly-sequenced standalone media-type fix that unblocks Claude vision.
B_best: Caught the streamed-plugin regression with raw chunk evidence and fixed it without dropping chunks (replaying what it consumed), then proved the bot's full seven paths run on gpt-6-luna and claude-haiku-5-5 by removing the hardcoded model tables — the actual gate on every model, price and Flex decision — and was honest that fallbacks cover nothing once a stream has started, which is this bot's default.
A_worst: Its migration branch leaves streamed plugin calls silently broken under the repo's default config, and its 'do nothing' verdict on prompt caching — contradicted by B's controlled A/B showing zero cached tokens without the key — risks abandoning the single biggest cost lever in an app that replays the whole conversation every turn.
B_worst: Shallower on the economics it hands to the human: d1 leaves the chat-model choice as an unranked decision with no per-call cost/latency comparison of the candidates, it never measures the tier question beyond noting gpt-4o has no Flex, and like A it never asks whether some of these calls (notably summarisation) need a model at all, nor touches spend caps, shadow models, Jev or Switchyard.
